title: Best Time to Visit Pompeii: Weather, Crowds & Queue Tips
metaTitle: Best Time to Visit Pompeii (2026 Guide: Avoid Crowds & Heat)
metaDescription: Discover the best time of day and month to visit Pompeii. Expert tips on avoiding crowds, beating the heat, and getting the most out of your visit.
excerpt: Opening vs. midday, the best months for thinner crowds, and why arriving right at opening completely changes your visit.
quickAnswer: Arrive right at 9:00 AM opening time and head straight for the Forum. You'll get the site at its quietest and coolest before tour groups and midday heat arrive.
imageAlt: Ancient Roman ruins under morning light

content.text: Pompeii is one of the most visited archaeological sites in the world, which means it can get busy — especially in peak summer season. The timing of your visit makes a real difference to how much you enjoy the site.
The Golden Rule: Opening Rush vs. Midday Crowds

Pompeii opens at 9:00 AM daily. Guests who arrive right at opening get the Forum and main streets noticeably quieter than those who arrive after 11:00 AM, once tour buses and later arrivals fill the site.
Best Months of the Year to Visit

Campania's climate is mild for much of the year, but Pompeii is busiest in July and August, when temperatures are high and there is very little shade on site. April, May, September, and October offer milder weather with noticeably thinner crowds.
Weekday vs. Weekend
Weekdays are generally quieter than weekends and Italian public holidays, when local visitors join the usual tourist crowd. If your schedule is flexible, a Tuesday or Wednesday visit is a good bet.
Summary & Recommendations

To get the most out of your visit, book your ticket online in advance, arrive right at 9:00 AM, bring water and sun protection, and prioritize the Forum and Amphitheatre first before the site fills up.

quickAnswer: If you enjoy exploring independently at your own pace, the skip-the-line ticket with audio guide is the better value. If you want an expert to bring the ruins to life and answer questions in real time, book the guided tour.

content.text: When booking your Pompeii visit, one of the first decisions is whether to go with the self-guided skip-the-line entrance ticket or upgrade to a guided tour with a licensed archaeologist.
Why the Guided Tour Wins for First-Time Visitors

Pompeii's ruins can be hard to interpret without context — a licensed archaeologist guide explains what you're looking at, points out details you'd otherwise walk past, and answers questions on the spot. For most first-time visitors, this transforms the visit.
When the Skip-the-Line Ticket Makes More Sense

If you prefer exploring at your own pace, want to linger at specific spots, or are visiting on a tighter budget, the skip-the-line ticket with the official audio guide covers the same must-see highlights at a lower price.
The Verdict
Book the guided tour if this is your first visit and you want expert context. Book the skip-the-line ticket if you're comfortable exploring independently or want more flexibility over your timing.

title: How to Get to Pompeii: Transport, Opening Hours & What to Pack
metaTitle: Getting to Pompeii: Transport, Hours & Packing List (2026)

quickAnswer: Pompeii is easiest to reach by the Circumvesuviana train to Pompei Scavi – Villa dei Misteri station, a 5-minute walk from the Porta Marina entrance, with direct trains from both Naples and Sorrento.

content.text: Getting to Pompeii

The Circumvesuviana train line connects Naples and Sorrento, stopping at Pompei Scavi – Villa dei Misteri station, a 5-minute walk from the Porta Marina entrance. From Naples, the journey takes about 35 minutes; from Sorrento, about 30 minutes. If you're visiting from Rome, take a high-speed train to Naples and connect to the Circumvesuviana, or book a guided day tour with return transport included.
Opening Hours by Season

In summer season (April 1 to October 31), Pompeii is open 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM daily, with last entry at 5:30 PM. In winter season (November 1 to March 31), it's open 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM daily, with last entry at 3:30 PM. The park is closed on January 1, May 1, and December 25.
Essential Packing Checklist

items: Comfortable, closed-toe walking shoes for uneven ancient stone paving
A hat and reef-safe sunscreen — there's very little shade on site
A refillable water bottle, especially in summer
A light jacket or layer for cooler months
A power bank if you're using your phone as an audio guide or camera

content.text: Make the Most of Your Day

Arrive right at opening, prioritize the Forum and Amphitheatre first, and pace yourself — Pompeii covers over 160 acres. If you have a full day in the region, consider the combo tour with Herculaneum and Mount Vesuvius to see all three sites at once.
